EXPLANATION IN PAPER
THE LOGIC:
Starter missions are the user’s safe starting point. Explorer increases the target. Trailblazer pushes consistency. Marathoner is the advanced cap for that BMI category.
This way, a user does not get random hard missions immediately. The missions increase only after the user proves consistency, which makes the app feel adaptive, fair, and less repetitive.
WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION
For the “real basis,” we can explain in your paper/defense that the missions are based on
WHO physical activity recommendations
WHO BMI classification
, and step-count research. WHO recommends adults do
150–300 minutes of moderate-intensity physical activity per week

, while WHO BMI classification identifies underweight, normal, overweight, and obesity categories. Since your app can only track walking, the missions translate those recommendations into progressive step goals. Studies also show that around
7,000 steps/day or more
is associated with lower mortality risk, and walking/step-monitoring interventions commonly increase activity by around
2,000–4,000 steps/day
over time.
